objective: Test segregation of duties in the procure-to-pay cycle — no single individual both requests and approves a purchase.
procedure_performed: Retrieved the full AP population for CTRL-02 (6 items, $87,700.00). Tested all items via test_items_against_control for segregation-of-duties violations (requestor == approver). Queried criteria_rag for POL-002 (Segregation of Duties Policy) and the synthetic standard on authorization assertions. Retrieved master record for E-211 to confirm role. Queried prior-year workpapers for CTRL-02 precedent.
population_summary: Source: LEDGER_DB. Account: AP. Period: 2025–2026. Population: 6 items. Total value: $87,700.00.
exceptions: TXN-011 | Atlas Training Solutions | $4,200.00 | segregation_of_duties — Requestor E-211 (HR Director) is the same person as approver E-211. Breaches POL-002 §2 Incompatible Function Pairs: 'Requesting a purchase / Approving the same purchase' must be performed by different individuals.
criteria_cited: POL-002 — Segregation of Duties Policy | §1 Purpose | No single individual performs incompatible functions within the procure-to-pay cycle.

POL-002 — Segregation of Duties Policy | §2 Incompatible Function Pairs | Requesting a purchase and approving the same purchase must be performed by different individuals. A transaction where the requestor and approver are the same person is a control deviation.
POL-002 — Segregation of Duties Policy | §3 System Enforcement | ERP system shall prevent same user ID from completing both functions; where not feasible, compensating detective control required.
Synthetic Audit Standard — Financial Statement Assertions | §S2 | Authorization: all transactions approved by personnel with appropriate authority.
prior_year_reference: WP-2024-002 | FY2024 | CTRL-02 | 0/142 (0%) — no SoD violations identified. NO EXCEPTION. Current finding is new — no prior precedent.
preliminary_conclusion: CTRL-02 exhibited one segregation-of-duties violation (TXN-011, 16.7% deviation rate). E-211 both requested and approved a $4,200 purchase from Atlas Training Solutions. This is a new finding with no prior-year precedent (WP-2024-002 found zero violations in FY2024). The auditor should assess whether compensating controls (supervisory review per POL-002 §4) were in place and whether the ERP system enforcement (POL-002 §3) failed or was bypassed.
judgment_note: The auditor must: (1) determine whether a compensating review was performed within 5 business days per POL-002 §4; (2) investigate whether the ERP system's SoD enforcement was bypassed or misconfigured for E-211's user profile; (3) assess whether this isolated violation represents a control design gap or an operational lapse; (4) determine the appropriate severity classification.
